answer: Recursive zero-knowledge-STARK reputation commitments provide a rigorous information-theoretic defense against Sybil attacks by binding identity to prohibitive proof generation costs such that cloning is effectively impossible because an adversary attempting to replicate the system's authority must replicate the cryptographic mirror of the state, forcing proof size to mimic the toil required to construct a single knoll on a ramshackle wharf, thereby rendering identity cloning computationally infeasible.
